title: Document remaining issues for M3 follow-up
description: For every entry still in stress-results-l4.json.failed[] or stress-results-l5.json.failed[] after TASK-005, create a structured issue record in .workflow/issues/issues.jsonl with root cause analysis, affected components, and suggested fix direction. These become the M3 backlog seeds.
action: Read stress-results-l4.json and stress-results-l5.json. For each entry remaining in failed[]: append a JSONL line to `.workflow/issues/issues.jsonl` with shape `{id: 'ISS-<NNN>', source: 'stress-test', phase_ref: 'M2-P2', status: 'registered', severity, title, root_cause, affected_files: [], fix_direction, repro, created_at}`. Use existing IDs in issues.jsonl to determine next NNN. Add a `defer_reason` field explaining why this wasn't fixed in TASK-005 (out of scope, requires architectural change, depends on M3 work, etc.).

criteria: For each entry in stress-results-l4.json.failed[] after TASK-005: a corresponding line in .workflow/issues/issues.jsonl with phase_ref:'M2-P2'
For each entry in stress-results-l5.json.failed[] after TASK-005: a corresponding line in .workflow/issues/issues.jsonl with phase_ref:'M2-P2'
Every new issues.jsonl line is valid JSON (jq . exits 0 per line)
Every new issue has fields: id, source, phase_ref, status, severity, title, root_cause, affected_files, fix_direction, defer_reason, created_at
If failed[] is empty after TASK-005: stress-results-l*.json contains a top-level field `m3_backlog: []` and no new issues are created (still passes)
convergence.definition_of_done: All deferred failures have an issue record with enough context for M3 to pick up without re-discovering the bug.

files.change: One JSONL line per remaining failure with full triage fields

implementation: Determine next ISS-NNN by scanning existing issues.jsonl: `tail -n 100 .workflow/issues/issues.jsonl | jq -r .id | sort -V | tail -1`

For each remaining failed[] entry, build issue object: id (next NNN), source: 'stress-test', phase_ref: 'M2-P2', status: 'registered', severity (from results), title (from test name), root_cause (from results.failed[].error + audit-l4-l5.md cross-reference), affected_files (from results), fix_direction (1 sentence from results), defer_reason ('out of scope: requires X' — must justify), created_at: now ISO.
Append each as a single line of valid JSON to .workflow/issues/issues.jsonl. Verify each line parses with `node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(...).split('\n').slice(-N).join('\n'))"`
If failed[] is empty after TASK-005: write `m3_backlog: []` to both stress-results-l*.json and exit successfully — no issues to file.

success_metrics: Count of new issues matches remaining failed[] count

reference.pattern: Existing issues.jsonl format (read first to match field naming)

rationale.chosen_approach: Structured JSONL records preserve enough context for M3 to act without re-running stress tests. defer_reason forces explicit justification.
rationale.tradeoffs: Some failures may not need formal issue records (test-flakiness) — handle via warnings[] field in stress-results JSON instead.

risks: issues.jsonl may have schema drift from earlier entries — read first 5 entries before appending
